 Automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 362 matching passages shared between the *Umaṅgajātaka* and 11 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive reuse occurs in the commentary, the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, which contains 236 matches in its sixth volume (such as segment range §147.1–160.4 matching commentary §3359_3–3402) and 30 matches in its seventh volume [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects substantial verse and textual overlap with other major narrative works in the collection, specifically the *Vidhurajātaka* (Ja 546, where segments §191.1–195.1 correspond to §317.1–321.1), the *Vessantarajātaka* (Ja 547), and the *Mūgapakkhajātaka* (Ja 538) [DharmaNexus]. Portions of the text are additionally cited or shared in grammatical works such as Aggavaṃsa's *Saddanītippakaraṇaṃ* (*Dhātumālā* and *Padamālā*) and Leḍī Sayāḍo's *Niruttidīpanīpāṭha* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-linguistic machine alignments, DharmaNexus detects low-to-moderate scoring matches with texts in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit, including the Chinese *Qishi yinben jing* (起世因本經, T 25), the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D 1), Kṣemendra's *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D 4155), the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (D 326), and the Sanskrit *Ajitasenavyākaraṇa* [DharmaNexus].
